newsitem.title: USA: DFSC gives details in fuel contract fraud case.
newsitem.headline: DFSC gives details in fuel contract fraud case.

text.p: The Defense Fuel Supply Center (DFSC), a U.S. Department of Defense agency, on Friday named the defendents in a fraud case in which the government was overbilled for millions of dollars worth of fuel in the early 1990s.

The DFSC in a statement said that International Marine Fuels of San Fransico Inc, KIMAC Enterprises Inc and Med-Atlantic Petroleum engaged in two separate bid-rigging and conspiracy schemes from 1990 to 1993, resulting in overpayment by DFSC offices of more than $28 million.
The DFSC previously hadn't named the defendents or the amount of the fraud.

"The defendants, John Santana, President of IMF, Keith Rasquinha, an independent broker, June King and Andrea McDonald, president and vice president of KIMAC, respectively, have pled guilty to violations which include tax evasion, aiding and abetting, conspiracy, making false statements and mail fraud," the DFSC said.
A prosecution was brought by the Assistant U.S. Attorneys in the District of New Jersey and a number of the defendents were sentenced to prison, probation and/or substantial fines in January, 1997.

The criminal and civil investigations are continuing and bankruptcy proceedings against Med-Atlantic Petroleum remain ongoing. No date has yet been set for sentencing of John Santana of IMF or Jackie Plecas of Med-Atlantic, DFSC said.

"We wanted people to know that the government is in the process of prosecuting a number of individuals and still looking, perhaps, at other possible abuses," said Cassandra Watson, a spokesperson for DFSC.

"We are still looking at what type of conspiracy occured and trying to make sure that this type of fraud doesn't occur again," she said, explaining the government's reason for releasing details of the case now.

The Department of Defense has centralized the payments system at DFAS Columbus, provided additional training for staff and made its tendering process more transparent in the wake of the fraud, the DFSC said.
